# Step 2: genomic prediction {#sec-prediction}

::: {.lead}
`02_genomic_prediction.Rmd` compares eight evaluation models for NUE, milk urea, Saved Feed and methane, to choose the model on evidence and to measure how well a low-heritability trait like NUE can be predicted.
:::

## The models

| Model | Idea |
|---|---|
| ABLUP | Pedigree only (baseline) |
| GBLUP | Genomic relationships, many small effects |
| ssGBLUP | Single-step: genotyped and non-genotyped animals together, pooled |
| ssGBLUP_MF | Single-step with breed metafounders |
| wssGBLUP | Weighted single-step |
| rrBLUP | Ridge regression on SNP effects |
| BayesA, BayesB | Allow some SNP to have large effects |

## How accuracy was measured

- **Validation.** Three-fold cross-validation, plus forward validation in which the youngest cows are predicted from older ones.
- **Accuracy** is the correlation between the estimated and the true breeding value. Only a simulation knows the true value.
- **Within-breed accuracy** is reported, because selection happens within breed. Pooled accuracy is distorted by differences between breed means.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Single-step in a multi-breed population
The genomic (G) and pedigree (A~22~) relationship matrices have different bases. Without adjustment, single-step GBLUP gives breed-level offsets in the breeding values. The pipeline tests an adjusted G and breed metafounders (Vitezica et al. 2011; Legarra et al. 2015).
:::

## What it found

Mean within-breed accuracy of each model (forward and k-fold validation):

{{< include _includes/cv_accuracy.md >}}

A single-step model was the best or within 0.05 of the best in 10 of 10 trait x validation comparisons. Differences below about 0.05 are within fold-to-fold noise. Weighted single-step gave over-dispersed breeding values.

Full reports: [NUE](../reports/02_genomic_prediction_FULL_rg1.00_NUE.html), [milk urea](../reports/02_genomic_prediction_FULL_rg1.00_MUN.html), [Saved Feed](../reports/02_genomic_prediction_FULL_rg1.00_SF.html), [methane](../reports/02_genomic_prediction_FULL_rg1.00_CH4.html).
